Data: CRU Analysis
Spot premium quotations for imported cathode continued to rise as the SHFE/LME cash month price ratio widened following the slump in the LME copper price. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode were in the US$120150/t range, whereas spot premium quotations for SXEW were quoted at between US$100-120/t. It has become apparent that traders and consumers are cautious to purchase imported cathode due to the tight credit market at the end of Q3. When SHFE re-opened after China’s week-long national holiday, the spot imported cathode market became more active. We estimate that there are now only around 250,000t of cathode in Shanghai bonded warehouses, with most of it being traders’ working inventory. Consumer stock levels also remain low due to tight credit availability. Consequently, we expect for Chinese cathode imports to rise to an average of over 200,000t/m in Q4, in order to meet contractual commitments and traders’ requirements. In terms of 2012 premium negotiations for imported cathode, some domestic market insiders expect that Codelco may cut premium charges to China amid news reports that the company plans to reduce premiums charged to European buyers next year by 8% as a result of a slowdown in developed © 2011 CRU International Limited **confidential** **October 2011** www.crumonitor.com economies. Most scrap traders are holding back material and are reluctant to sell at the moment to avoid losses. We noticed that the discount for No.1 scrap turned into a premium to cathode since the end of August. As a result, it is currently difficult for scrap users to purchase material needed to maintain their operations. In fact, some secondary smelters and low oxygen wirerod producers have cut back or even suspended operations due to a lack of material. We believe that the tight scrap supply will last for an extended period of time, as traders’ scrap import enthusiasm is constrained by the expectation of copper prices remaining volatile, altho

ugh improvements in the SHFE/LME price ratio may benefit scrap imports. In the medium term, the scrap market may tighten further if Europe falls into industrial recession. Additionally, wire and cable producers would like to purchase more oxygen free wirerod instead of low oxygen wirerod, meaning that scrap supply tightness should boost refined copper demand. The boost to cathode demand may also come from reduced secondary refined production. # **SGCC reinforced smart grid development plan in 2011-2015** The 2011 Smart Grid International Forum was held in Beijing on 28th -29th September by the State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) and the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE). The General Manager of the SGCC announced their reinforced smart grid development plans from 2011 to 2015. According to his presentation, the ultra high-voltage power grids and smart power grid developments are part of China’s Twelfth Five-Year Plan, leading us to believe that they will further boost future copper demand. The SGCC will strengthen the reinforced smart grid construction in the coming five years, by building a "three vertical and three horizontal" structured UHV power grid; creating highly intelligent transmission and distribution networks; constructing 6,100 intelligent substations of 110kV and above; building 2,900 units of new electric vehicle charging stations and 540,000 charge piles; and by installing 230 million smart meters. By 2015, the resource allocation capabilities, security capabilities and the public service capacity of the SGCC will be fully improved. In the first week of October, the LME 3-month copper price rallied, driven by the improved U.S. and Chinese economic data. However, the euro-zone debt crisis escalation remains the big concern for market participants despite assurances of support from the ECB, France and Germany. On the first day of trading after the week-long national holiday, the SHFE 3-month copper price closed at RMB54,480/t, down 0.8% from 30th September. At the same time, we noticed that there is currently a modest premium in the Shanghai physical market, with most consumers still cautious and not actively purchasin

g cathode.  In its third quarter meeting, China’s Central Bank was quoted as saying "inflation pressures have eased," however, their strategy of "implementing prudent monetary policy to stabilize the general price level" indicates that the current trend of tightening monetary policy will continue. We believe that in the short term the copper price will be supported by the decline in exchange stocks. However, the euro-zone debt crisis will continue to constrain the copper price rally. We predict that the SHFE 3-month copper price will fluctuate between RMB52,000-55,000/t over the next two weeks.
